records.name: Appalachian Mountain Club, Delaware Valley Chapter
records.summary: Outdoor club that runs hundreds of trips a year around Philadelphia and nearby areas: hikes, paddling, biking, backpacking and trail work days. Most trips are free and led by trained leaders.
records.what_you_do: Join a hike, paddle or bike ride led by a trained leader, or help with trail work days.

schedule.text: Trips and events run through the year and are listed on the activity calendar

cost.text: Most activities are free, according to the chapter's home page. Check each listing.

first_step.how: Browse the activity calendar on the chapter site and sign up for a trip that suits your level
first_step.basis: Trips are listed publicly and led by trained leaders. The home page does not say membership is required for trips, though it promotes joining.

records.notes: The activity calendar is hosted on another site (AMC Outdoors Connector) that I could not read, so no dated trip is recorded. The pages I read show no dated event or news item. A fall 2026 newsletter file is linked, but the date comes from the file path, not an event, so status is probably_active. Membership offers, a 20s and 30s group and a Lehigh Valley group are also run under this chapter; not recorded separately. The contact page shows a contact button but no phone or mailing address.

records.name: Philadelphia Canoe Club
records.summary: Paddling club that has taught and promoted paddle sports in Philadelphia since 1905. It runs lessons in kayak, canoe, stand-up paddleboard and pool sessions, plus trips open to the public.
records.what_you_do: Take a lesson, join a trip, or come to the monthly club meeting.

schedule.text: Monthly club meeting on the third Monday at 7:30 pm, with lessons and trips through the year

cost.text: Lesson and membership prices were not on the pages I read.

first_step.how: Sign up for a lesson or trip through the club site, or join its mailing list. Trips, training and events do not require membership.
first_step.basis: The club runs beginner-level lessons across several paddle types and says trips and training are open to the public without membership.

records.notes: The home page lists a monthly club meeting marked session 12 of 50, dated 18 January 2027, so the meeting series is running. The page shows no posting dates, so last_sign_of_life uses the date I read it. The page does not state a minimum age or guest policy. It links to a membership levels page that I did not read. A phone number came up in search results but is not on the page I read, so it is left out.

records.name: Friends of the Wissahickon
records.summary: Nonprofit that cares for Wissahickon Valley Park in Philadelphia. Volunteers join service days, trail crews, clean-ups and habitat monitoring, and trained volunteers lead guided walks.
records.what_you_do: Join a service day to help maintain trails and habitat, or train as a crew leader or guided walk volunteer.

schedule.text: Volunteer service days run on a regular weekly schedule. The Thursday service day meets at Thomas Mill Red Covered Bridge. Guided hikes are listed on the events page.

locations.label: Thomas Mill Red Covered Bridge (Thursday service day meeting point)

cost.text: The cost of volunteering or joining a guided walk was not stated on the pages I read.

first_step.how: Find a service day or guided hike on the events page and register through it. The office can answer questions by phone.
first_step.basis: Service days and guided hikes are posted publicly with a registration step, but the page did not say whether beginners need experience or what to bring.

records.notes: The name Wissahickon Trails did not match any separate group in search, so this record is for Friends of the Wissahickon, the group that does this work. The home page shows an article dated 8 October 2026, which sets the status. The page publishes no email address. The park is listed at about 2,000 acres. Search results mentioned Wednesday, Saturday and Sunday service days and free guided hikes, but I could not confirm them on the group's pages, so they are left out.

records.name: Batona Hiking Club
records.summary: Hiking club that runs group hikes, trail upkeep days and an annual dinner. Its upcoming meeting points are in the suburbs and state forests outside Philadelphia.
records.notes: Judgment call for the owner. Every upcoming meeting point on the club's site is outside Philadelphia: King of Prussia, Ridley Creek, Phoenixville, Springfield, Chester County, and state forests farther away. The site also lists a past hike at a Philadelphia ZIP code (19118, the Wissahickon), so the club does touch the city. I set out_of_area because it does not meet in the city now. Flip to publish if the owner wants suburban clubs with Philadelphia members. Hikes cost one dollar each and most need an RSVP. Leader and organizer contact details are not recorded. The fetch read the first 100,000 characters of a 113,876 character page.

records.summary: Local Sierra Club group for Philadelphia and four nearby counties that works on environmental issues and runs free outings, including day hikes, paddling and bird walks.
records.what_you_do: Join a free outing, help lead one, or use the group's volunteer interest form to get connected with a leader.

cost.text: Outings are free, according to the group's pages as quoted in search results.

first_step.how: Use the group's volunteer interest form or check its outings listings to find a trip
first_step.basis: Outings are advertised publicly with a sign-up route. The group's page could not be read, so this rests on search summaries of it.

records.notes: The group's own pages came back empty to my fetch tool, so the summary, cost and sign-up route come from search results that quote the group's site. They are not checked against a readable page. The newest dated item I could find is a July 2023 blog post, which makes the status dormant under our rule, but the live site may be current. Please check the group's pages in a browser before publishing. Search results give two different Executive Committee meeting times, so none is recorded. The group names Philadelphia, Delaware, Chester, Montgomery and Bucks counties as its area.
